channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan Discussed as Responsible Middle Power at ISMI Seminar
item.description: The Institute for Strategic and Regional Studies (ISMI) hosted a seminar on Uzbekistan's emergence as a responsible middle power, marking the country's 35th independence anniversary. The event focused on a new analytical report detailing the evolution of Uzbekistan's foreign policy, particularly its increased openness and initiative in the last decade, while maintaining core principles.

item.title: Memorandum Signed to Explore Renewable Energy Projects in Uzbekistan
item.description: Saudi company ACWA Power and South Korean Korea Western Power Co., Ltd. (KOWEPO) signed a memorandum in Tashkent to study renewable energy potential in Uzbekistan. The agreement aims to jointly assess opportunities in renewable energy, energy storage systems, and related infrastructure, potentially attracting South Korean investment.

item.title: Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan Share Common Regional Strategic Interests, Official States
item.description: Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan are united by common regional strategic interests, according to an Azerbaijani Member of Parliament. He stated that bilateral relations have moved beyond traditional cooperation to become a significant component of broader regional processes. The relationship is built on political trust, economic complementarity, and spiritual closeness.

item.title: Teenager with Schizophrenia on Trial in Aktobe for Mother's Murder
item.description: A 16-year-old teenager diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia is on trial in Aktobe for allegedly murdering his mother and injuring his grandmother. Specialists concluded he was not aware of his actions during the crime, which reportedly stemmed from a prolonged family conflict. He confessed to the charges.

item.title: New Gas Block Production Plant Launched in Uzbekistan's Fergana Region
item.description: A new gas block production plant has been launched in the Dangara district of Uzbekistan's Fergana region. The project, implemented with $40 million in foreign investment, is equipped with advanced technologies and has created 80 new jobs. This initiative expands production capacity in the building materials sector.

item.title: Russia Plans Escalation of Ukraine Conflict, Potentially Targeting Kyiv, Bloomberg Reports
item.description: Russian authorities are planning a new escalation of the war against Ukraine, potentially involving ballistic missile strikes on central Kyiv and energy infrastructure, according to Bloomberg, citing sources close to the Kremlin. The decision reportedly stems from Russian President Vladimir Putin's assessment of a stalemate in negotiations.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans Expansion of Pistachio Plantations in Arid Zones with Iranian Expertise
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to establish large pistachio plantations in arid and semi-arid steppe zones, covering over 32 million hectares. Fifty Iranian specialists have been invited to assess land suitability and introduce high-yield, low-growing pistachio varieties. Drip irrigation technology will be used, with potential for significant economic returns.

item.title: Uzbekistan focuses on crime prevention in local communities
item.description: Uzbekistan is implementing new mechanisms for analyzing crime situations and predicting criminal activity within its internal affairs bodies. The head of state has prioritized timely prevention of offenses in every neighborhood. This approach shifts focus from solely law enforcement to a broader responsibility involving employment, education, healthcare, and local authorities in addressing crime-generating factors.

item.title: Foreign national arrested in Osh for attempting to bribe police officer
item.description: A foreign national has been detained in Osh, Kyrgyzstan, for attempting to bribe a police officer. The individual, born in 1980, was found to be working in the city without proper registration or permits. After being informed about the need for legal documents, he offered a bribe to the officer to avoid legal consequences and continue his illegal stay.

item.title: 232 Kazakh citizens awarded 'Bolashak' scholarship for international studies
item.description: A total of 232 Kazakh citizens have been awarded the 'Bolashak' scholarship for international studies. Of these, 179 will pursue master's degrees, 12 doctoral degrees, one a bachelor's degree, and 40 will undertake professional internships abroad. Additionally, 33 individuals received scholarships for scientific internships. The lists of recipients will be published on August 27.

item.title: Tashkent University of Applied Sciences expands international cooperation in higher education
item.description: Tashkent University of Applied Sciences (TAFU), celebrating its fifth anniversary, is among the top five private institutions in Uzbekistan whose graduates receive state-standard diplomas. The university currently enrolls over 20,000 students taught by more than 500 professors. TAFU aims to prepare specialists capable of working internationally, emphasizing the importance of qualified faculty and foreign language proficiency.

item.title: Bishkek to Close Chuy Avenue for Two Days for Major Events
item.description: A section of Chuy Avenue in Bishkek will be closed to traffic from August 27 to August 29. The closure is to ensure security during the upcoming World Nomad Games and the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit. Authorities have requested drivers to plan alternative routes.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Singapore Sign Agreements on Water, Transport, and Trade Cooperation
item.description: Kazakhstan and Singapore have agreed to cooperate in water management, transport, and trade. Agreements were signed during a meeting between President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Singapore's Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong. Bilateral trade neared one billion dollars last year, with Singaporean FDI doubling.

item.title: First Paid Road in Uzbekistan, Urgench-Khiva, Costs Increased to $150 Million
item.description: The construction cost of Uzbekistan's first paid road, connecting Urgench and Khiva, has risen from $120 million to $150 million. The 35-kilometer, four-lane highway is expected to boost regional tourism. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev noted this as the first paid road experience in Uzbekistan.

item.title: Chinese Expert Praises Uzbekistan's Reforms and Development
item.description: Ma Bin, director of Fudan University's Center for Russian and Central Asian Studies, congratulated Uzbekistan on its upcoming 35th Independence Day. He highlighted the 'New Uzbekistan' model, emphasizing reforms in politics, economy, and foreign policy since 2016, which have led to significant changes.

item.title: Uzbek President Awards State Decorations for 35 Years of Independence
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev presented state awards to citizens for achievements during Uzbekistan's 35 years of independence. He highlighted the nation's progress, noting over $160 billion in foreign investment and a 2.5-fold economic growth in the past decade. The president also mentioned the creation of millions of jobs and significant infrastructure development, including schools, hospitals, and roads.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Initiatives within SCO Focus on Economy and Security
item.description: Uzbekistan actively contributes to the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO), focusing on security, trade, economic cooperation, industrial and technological collaboration, cultural ties, and regional connectivity. The SCO has grown from six founding members to ten, with significant interest from other nations. Uzbekistan's trade turnover with SCO members reached $81.2 billion in 2025.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's 'Kyrgyzpharma' may store humanitarian aid and state procurement medicines
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Health proposes transferring the storage and distribution of medicines from humanitarian aid and state procurement to the state enterprise 'Kyrgyzpharma'. Currently, the Department of Medicines and Medical Devices handles these functions. The proposed change aims to separate regulatory and operational roles within the ministry's subordinate organizations.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Economy Ministry proposes changes to deposit protection rules
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Economy and Commerce has proposed amendments to the Law 'On Protection of Bank Deposits'. The current system, unchanged since 2008, faces challenges as deposit volumes have grown significantly faster than the insurance fund. The ministry suggests new, risk-based contribution rates for banks and microfinance organizations to strengthen the deposit protection fund.

item.title: Navoiy region imports labor from other Uzbek regions, says governor
item.description: Navoiy region governor Normat Tursunov stated that over 50,000 people from other regions of Uzbekistan are working in Navoiy. He linked this labor import to the region's economic development and the creation of new production capacities. The governor also reported on the launch of a 300 MW solar generation project and a 150 MW energy storage project in Nurata district.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Acquires 9 Hectares in Xi'an for Transport and Logistics Center
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is acquiring a 9-hectare land plot in Xi'an, China, to establish a transport and logistics center. This center will be part of the Xi'an-Kashgar-Osh multimodal route, facilitating cargo transport via rail and road. The project aims to launch new routes and increase freight volumes before the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway is completed.

item.title: Uzbekneftegaz to Strengthen Control Over Joint Ventures Amid Production Decline and Dividend Issues
item.description: Uzbekneftegaz has begun systematically inspecting and increasing control over its joint ventures due to declining production volumes and issues with dividend payments. The company cited insufficient operational regulation, lack of transparency in accounting, and unfulfilled dividend obligations as problems. This intensified oversight aims to address these systemic issues.

item.title: Uzbek President States Lack of Political Will Led to Cotton 'Slavery'
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev stated that a lack of political will previously led to Uzbekistan's near-total focus on cotton cultivation, involving schoolchildren in field labor. He noted that this "cotton slavery" dominated all aspects of state and public life for much of the year. The president's remarks were made during a ceremony in the Syrdarya region.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Modifies 'Uyi-bulogo Komok' Benefit Criteria Effective September 1
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet of Ministers has amended the criteria for the 'uyi-bulogo komok' monthly benefit for families with children under 16, effective September 1, 2026. Changes include increasing the guaranteed minimum income threshold and introducing new criteria, such as limiting eligibility for families owning cars older than 15 years or multiple properties.

item.title: Uzbekistan discusses strengthening public-private partnerships against digital terrorism
item.description: A two-day seminar was held at the Academy of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Uzbekistan to enhance cooperation between law enforcement and tech companies in combating digital terrorism. Organized within the framework of the Uzbekistan-ITU Roadmap, the event focused on improving state-private sector interaction against the use of new technologies for terrorism, responding to online incidents, and conducting investigations. Disruptive groups are increasingly using digital services for radicalization and recruitment.

item.title: Uzbekistan's business environment evolved over 35 years of independence
item.description: Over 35 years of independence, Uzbekistan has transitioned from a Soviet-type economy to a model emphasizing private property, entrepreneurship, and market competition. This economic transformation occurred in stages: foundation of the national economy (1991-1996), gradual development of small businesses (1997-2016), large-scale liberalization (since 2017), and the current phase focused on reducing state role, privatization, tax reforms, and digitalization.

item.title: Kyrgyz journalist Mahabat Tazhybek kyzy denied travel to receive award from Clooney
item.description: A court in Bishkek denied Kyrgyz journalist Mahabat Tazhybek kyzy permission to travel to London to receive an award from George Clooney. The journalist stated she does her work for progress and legality, not for awards. The Committee to Protect Journalists and the International Press Institute have called on Kyrgyzstan to drop charges against her and allow her to work freely.

item.title: Uzbekistan Presents New Ecological Initiatives Focused on Nature Restoration at UN Conference
item.description: Uzbekistan showcased new ecological initiatives at a UN conference in Ulaanbaatar, focusing on degraded land restoration and climate resilience. Advisor to the President Aziz Abdukhakimov highlighted successful investments in Karakalpakstan, including a project funded by the Abu Dhabi Fund for Development. The initiative aimed to develop sustainable agricultural systems in degraded areas.

item.title: Uzbekistan Inaugurates 163 New Facilities Ahead of Independence Day Celebrations
item.description: Uzbekistan has commissioned 163 new facilities nationwide in anticipation of the 35th anniversary of its independence. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev highlighted reforms over the past decade, leading to a 2.5-fold economic increase, $160 billion in foreign investment, and creation of nearly 6 million jobs. The country is building the foundation for a 'Third Renaissance'.

item.title: Kazakhstan Police Implement New Rules for Electric Scooters, Banning Sidewalk Use
item.description: As of August 25, electric scooters are prohibited from riding on sidewalks and pedestrian paths in Kazakhstan. Police will monitor compliance using surveillance cameras, technical devices, and drones. Mobile police units on scooters will also patrol high-traffic areas. This measure follows 139 accidents involving electric scooters this year, resulting in two fatalities.

item.title: Uzbekistan Enhances Citizen Complaint System in the Energy Sector
item.description: Uzbekistan is improving its system for handling citizen complaints within the energy sector through a training seminar. The event focused on timely problem identification, effective solutions, and individual approaches to each appeal. Participants learned to enhance communication, manage complex situations, and adhere to service ethics and anti-corruption measures.

item.title: Central Asia International Educational Forum Preparation Underway in Tashkent
item.description: Tashkent will host the Central Asia International Educational Forum from October 27-30. A coordination meeting involving the Ministry of Higher Education, Science, and Innovation and leading universities discussed preparations and task distribution. A step-by-step action plan was approved to ensure a high-level organization and strengthen inter-university cooperation.

item.title: Uzbekistan and IMF Discuss Fiscal Policy and Public Finance Management Reforms
item.description: Uzbekistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Economy and Finance, Jamshid Kuchkarov, met with IMF Fiscal Department economist Amanda Sayegh. They discussed reforms to enhance fiscal policy and public finance management, focusing on risk identification, budget planning, and efficient resource utilization. Both sides agreed to continue practical exchanges.

item.title: Uzbekistan and USA Elevate Bilateral Relations to Strategic Partnership Level
item.description: A delegation from the US House of Representatives met with the Senate of Uzbekistan's Oliy Majlis. It was emphasized that bilateral relations have reached the level of strategic partnership due to the political will of leaders. Inter-parliamentary dialogue and cooperation in political, economic, and humanitarian spheres were highlighted as key to strengthening ties.

item.title: Uzbekistan and New Zealand Exchange Experience in Deposit Guarantee Systems
item.description: Uzbekistan's Deposit Insurance Agency held a video conference with New Zealand's Depositor Compensation Scheme (DCS). DCS representatives presented information on their system's operations, payout mechanisms, and public engagement strategies. Uzbekistan shared its practical experience, including a case study of a bank license revocation.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Kurultai Elections: Five Parties Secure Parliamentary Seats
item.description: Kazakhstan's Central Election Commission announced the results of the Kurultai elections, with five out of seven participating parties securing seats in the new parliament. The 'Adilet' party won decisively with 71.17% of the vote. Voter turnout was 74.08%. All parties support the president's political course.

item.title: US Kok-Boru team arrives in Kyrgyzstan for World Nomad Games
item.description: The US national team for Kok-Boru, consisting of nine players, arrived in Bishkek on August 25 to participate in the VI World Nomad Games. The team visited Bishkek Arena, where the opening ceremony will take place on August 31. After a day in Bishkek, the athletes will travel to Cholpon-Ata for training sessions.

item.title: US dollar exchange rate in Uzbekistan hits lowest point since August 2023
item.description: The official exchange rate for the US dollar in Uzbekistan fell to 11,778.52 som on August 26, marking its lowest point since a sharp depreciation of the som in August 2023. The Central Bank reported that the dollar weakened by 39.55 som in Tuesday's trading. Economists note the som's strengthening is occurring against a global trend of dollar weakening.
